title: Room finder and booking UI
idea: The booking frontend is a room finder plus a booking dialog, driven by one reducer, so a slow network or double click can never book twice.
points: `RoomFinderPage` owns the reducer; `TimeRangePicker`, `RoomList` and `BookingDialog` render it.
SUBMIT is ignored while SUBMITTING, and the key survives a network retry.
A 409 removes that room from the list and asks for another pick.
Follow-ups: live calendar updates, recurring series, and a room panel for check-in.

code.title: Booking screen reducer
code.caption: Pure screen logic. Run it, then add a third SUBMIT before BOOK_OK and predict the output.

walk.text: The whole screen state: step, rooms, chosen room, Idempotency-Key and error.
A new search resets everything; an empty result gets its own EMPTY step.
Picking another room drops the key; re-picking the same room keeps it.
SUBMIT works only from RESULTS; an existing key wins over the new one.
A 409 removes the taken room and clears the choice and key; no rooms left means EMPTY.
A network failure keeps the key, so the retry is safe to repeat.
Double click, conflict, failure, retry. Each `submit()` makes its key up front; the ignored click used bk-2.

code.title: BookingDialog component
code.caption: A React component that renders state, dispatches events, and sends the request when the step becomes SUBMITTING. Not run here.

walk.text: The request runs once per entry into SUBMITTING, with the reducer's key.
409 means BOOK_CONFLICT, 2xx BOOK_OK, else BOOK_FAILED; a real client gives 4xx its own message.
Loading and empty results get their own screens, never a blank list.
Submit passes a fresh UUID; the reducer ignores it when a key exists.
The button is disabled with no room or while a request is in flight.

pitfalls: A disabled button alone is not enough; the reducer must also ignore repeat submits.
Show times in the room's time zone; the API stores instants in UTC.
Interview follow-up: polling room lists at scale is costly; mention push updates or short caching.

quiz.q: In the run, what is the key after the retry SUBMIT?
quiz.why: SUBMIT keeps an existing key. BOOK_FAILED did not clear bk-3, so the retry ignores newKey bk-4 and reuses bk-3.

takeaway: One reducer, one key per attempt, and the server decides conflicts.

starters: Should the room list update live when someone else books?
Why is the key created in the event and not in the reducer?
How would the UI handle a recurring series with one conflict?
